staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged htslib checkout. The benchmark metadata's vulnerable/fixed commit pair refers to the htscodecs submodule (`dca826...` -> `cf8eca...`), while the line map used below is the live top-level htslib tree above with that vulnerable submodule checked out.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491972 (htslib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hts_open_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491972
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 138-byte witness is a malformed CRAM 2.0 file that reaches `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` for the first container. `cram_read_block()` parses that first header block with compression method `ARITH_PR0`; the saved ASan allocation stack at `cram_read_block:1445` shows `b->comp_size = 6`, so the block's compressed payload occupies a 6-byte heap region. `cram_uncompress_block()` passes that 6-byte buffer to `arith_uncompress_to()`, which first materializes `in_end = in + in_size` and then takes the striped path (`*in & X_STRIPE`). Inside that branch, `c_meta_len` starts at 1 and the bounded `var_get_u32(in+c_meta_len, in_end, &ulen)` consumes the remaining 5 bytes, advancing `c_meta_len` to exactly `in_size` before any output allocation or recursion occurs. The vulnerable code then immediately executes `unsigned int N = in[c_meta_len++]` without first checking that another byte exists. That read dereferences `in[6]`, one byte past the 6-byte block, and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `arith_uncompress_to`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by returning `NULL` when `c_meta_len >= in_size` after the `ulen` varint decode.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled block-header bytes into decompressor dispatch state.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 138-byte CRAM 2.0 file. The saved crash stack later enters `cram_uncompress_block()`'s `ARITH_PR0` case and then `arith_uncompress_to()`, so this statement materializes `b->method = ARITH_PR0` for the first SAM-header block on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: The striped-header decoder assumes `var_get_u32()` left at least one more byte for `N` and immediately indexes `in[c_meta_len]` without checking `c_meta_len < in_size`. On the witness, `c_meta_len` already equals `in_size`, so this line reads one byte past the compressed block.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (c_meta_len >= in_size) return NULL;` immediately before this line.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. This statement reads the stripe-count byte from `in[c_meta_len]`; with `c_meta_len == in_size == 6`, it dereferences the first byte past the 6-byte heap buffer allocated for the compressed block.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `arith_dynamic.c:931` on address `0x602000004c36`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x602000004c30, 0x602000004c36)` allocated at `cram_read_block:1445`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This bounded varint parse uses `in_end = in + in_size` as the only upper bound on the striped metadata decode. On the witness it consumes the 5 bytes from `in[1]` through `in[5]`, advancing `c_meta_len` from 1 to 6, which is the out-of-range index used by the next line.

parser_admitted.description: The input has already been admitted as CRAM, the first container reported at least one block, `cram_read_block()` succeeded, and `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` is now decompressing that first header block instead of aborting earlier.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, and reproduction report only.

Stage 02 does not build or execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing `c_meta_len >= in_size` guard before the crashing read.

The surrounding CRAM container/header bytes are themselves malformed enough that a manual static byte-to-offset reconstruction of the first block is not reliable without reusing htslib's live parser. This GT therefore grounds the 6-byte block size and first-block selection in the saved ASan allocation/call stacks rather than an offset-specific block dump.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the staged 138-byte witness in an in-memory file and calls `hts_hopen()`, which recognizes CRAM and enters `cram_dopen()` / `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` on attacker-controlled bytes.

The first SAM-header block header is parsed with compression method `ARITH_PR0`; `cram_read_block()` materializes `b->comp_size = 6`, allocates a 6-byte heap buffer, and reads the compressed payload into it.
Because the block method is `ARITH_PR0`, `cram_uncompress_block()` forwards that 6-byte payload to `arith_uncompress_to()`, where the first byte selects the striped-header decoder.

The striped `ulen` varint consumes the remaining 5 bytes of the 6-byte buffer, but the code never checks that another byte remains before reading `N`; `in[c_meta_len++]` therefore overreads one byte past the heap block and ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. `cram_read_block()` reads the current block's compression-method byte from the attacker-controlled CRAM stream. The saved crash stack later enters `cram_uncompress_block()`'s `case ARITH_PR0`, so this byte materializes `b->method = ARITH_PR0` for the crashing header block.

The same block header next materializes `b->comp_size`. On the witness this value is 6: `cram_read_block()` later mallocs 6 bytes at line 1445, and ASan reports the crashed address is 0 bytes to the right of that 6-byte region.

fine_trace.code:
if (!(b->data = malloc(b->comp_size)))  { free(b); return NULL; }
if (b->comp_size != hread(fd->fp, b->data, b->comp_size)) {
fine_trace.note: Because `b->method != RAW`, `cram_read_block()` executes the compressed-block `else` arm, allocates `b->comp_size` bytes, and reads that many attacker-controlled bytes into `b->data`. This heap region is the one ASan later reports as `[0x602000004c30, 0x602000004c36)`.

`cram_uncompress_block()` dispatches the block through its `ARITH_PR0` switch arm and passes the same `b->data` / `b->comp_size` pair into `arith_uncompress_to()`. The saved stack `arith_uncompress_to -> cram_uncompress_block -> cram_read_SAM_hdr` is the proof that this control arm was taken.

`arith_uncompress_to()` first materializes `in_end` as the one-past-end pointer for the 6-byte compressed-block buffer. This is the upper bound later passed into the striped-header `var_get_u32()` call.

fine_trace.code:
if (*in & X_STRIPE) {
    unsigned int ulen, olen, c_meta_len = 1;
fine_trace.note: The first compressed byte has `X_STRIPE` set, so execution enters the striped-header branch and initializes `c_meta_len = 1`. The next metadata decode therefore starts at `in + 1` inside the same 6-byte input buffer.

The bounded varint parse uses the `in + 1` start offset from step 6 and the `in_end` bound from step 5. This is the only statement before the sink that changes `c_meta_len`; because the next line overreads `in[6]` from a 6-byte buffer, the witness makes this call consume bytes `in[1..5]` and advance `c_meta_len` from 1 to 6.

Root cause and sink. No check enforces `c_meta_len < in_size` after the varint parse. With the same 6-byte `in` buffer from step 4 and `c_meta_len == 6` from step 7, `in[c_meta_len++]` dereferences `in[6]`, the first byte past the heap allocation. The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `arith_dynamic.c:931` on address `0x602000004c36`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x602000004c30, 0x602000004c36)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the exact missing `c_meta_len >= in_size` check before the crashing read, but Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 138-byte CRAM 2.0 file. On the crashing path, its first SAM-header block is parsed as an `ARITH_PR0` block with `b->comp_size = 6`; inside `arith_uncompress_to()`, the striped-header `ulen` varint consumes the remaining 5 bytes so the subsequent `N` read occurs at `in[6]`, one byte past the block.

format.name: CRAM 2.0
format.contract: A CRAM 2.0 file whose first SAM-header block reaches `cram_uncompress_block()` as an `ARITH_PR0` block with `b->comp_size = 6`, and whose 6-byte arithmetic payload takes the striped branch (`*in & X_STRIPE`) while `var_get_u32()` consumes bytes `in[1..5]`, leaving no remaining byte for `N`. That exact truncated striped-header layout makes `arith_uncompress_to()` read `in[6]` one byte past the heap block.
